1. Verify current-bill arithmetic: confirm meter reads (13,069 − 12,232 = 837 kWh), line-item sum ($18.38 + $22.02 + $112.50 = $152.90), and the total change versus last month ($152.90 − $166.88 = −$13.98). Flag any internal mismatch as a possible billing error.

2. Confirm both billing periods fall under the same AEP Ohio RS tariff (fixed $18.38/month; tier-1 variable $0.0263125 + $0.13441 = $0.1607225/kWh). Since rates are unchanged, set price_usd = $0.00. Both periods are 31 days and the customer charge is a flat monthly fee while energy/riders are billed per kWh, so set days_usd = $0.00.

3. Estimate weather_usd: from NOAA history, compare last month (HDD 1020, CDD 0, 924 kWh) with the current period (HDD 980.5, CDD 0, 837 kWh). Derive the weather-attributable kWh difference for this heating season and value it at the effective variable rate (~$0.1607/kWh).

4. Compute usage_usd as the residual so price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd = −$13.98 exactly (i.e., value the non-weather kWh change at the variable rate).

5. Screen for a billing error: reconstruct the tariff total for 837 kWh ($18.38 + 837 × $0.1607225 ≈ $152.90), compare to the stated $152.90 and line items, and verify kWh against meter reads; the match is within normal rounding, so billing_error_suspected = false and billing_error_usd = null.

6. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
